Datenschutz.title: Privacy Policy
Datenschutz.intro: Protecting your data is a top priority for ONCOcurve. This statement describes how the application handles data.
Datenschutz.localBody: ONCOcurve processes all uploaded files (oBDS XML, CSV, Excel) exclusively locally in your browser. All computations (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox regression) run on your device. No patient or case data is transmitted to any server or third party.
Datenschutz.noTransferBody: The application does not send any uploaded data to the internet. There are no uploads, no external API calls and no transfer to third parties.
Datenschutz.storageBody: Settings and selections (e.g. plot options, excluded cases) are kept only in your browser's session storage (sessionStorage) and are deleted when the tab is closed. No cookies are set for tracking purposes.
Datenschutz.trackingBody: ONCOcurve uses no analytics or tracking services (no Google Analytics, Matomo, etc.) and embeds no external fonts or scripts that could transmit your IP address to third parties.
Datenschutz.hostingBody: The application is served over an encrypted HTTPS connection. Because processing happens entirely in the browser, the server never receives patient data.
Datenschutz.responsibleBody: The entity named in the imprint is responsible for operating the service. For data-protection questions please use the contact details provided there.
Datenschutz.rightsBody: Because ONCOcurve neither transmits personal data to the operator nor stores it there, no processing by the operator takes place in that respect. Your institution remains responsible for the data you process locally; data-subject rights (Art. 15-21 GDPR) are directed to the processing entity.
Datenschutz.purposeBody: ONCOcurve is a tool for aggregated, retrospective cohort-level survival statistics (e.g. for clinical cancer registries and research). It is not intended to make or support diagnostic, prognostic or treatment decisions for individual patients, and is not a medical device within the meaning of Regulations (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) or 2017/746 (IVDR).

pHacking.tooltip: The p-value applies to this one question only. Trying several stratifications or filters and then reporting the smallest p-value turns pure chance into “significant” differences. Fix the question in advance, or label the finding explicitly as exploratory.

followUp.reverseKmTooltip: This figure estimates the cohort's average length of observation, correctly counting in the cases still being followed without an event (censoring). It is the methodologically standard way to state a study's follow-up time, shown as the annotation in the chart above. It differs from the figure next to it because that one is simply the midpoint of every observed time, without that adjustment.
followUp.tooltip: Plain median of the observed follow-up times, without accounting for censoring. Some certification sheets require exactly this figure. The reverse Kaplan-Meier estimate next to it accounts for censoring and therefore usually differs slightly.

export.heading: Export scope
export.tipFull: All data unchanged, including real patient IDs and treatment dates. For internal use only.
export.tipNoPatients: The patient table is omitted entirely. Survival curves, statistics and Cox analysis remain fully included. Details about the source file are removed.
export.tipPseudonymized: Patient IDs are replaced by P0001, P0002 … Diagnosis and end dates are shifted per patient by up to ±4 weeks; survival time stays exactly intact. Details about the source file are removed.
export.noteAnonymized: Pseudonymised: patient IDs replaced, diagnosis and end dates shifted per patient by up to ±4 weeks.
export.noteNoPatients: The patient table was deliberately removed from this export. All analyses, curves and statistics are based on the complete dataset.
export.noteOriginalData: All analyses in this report - survival curves, log-rank test and Cox analysis - were computed on the unmodified original data. Pseudonymisation was applied afterwards, to the printed patient table only.
export.noteYearBoundary: Note: if a diagnosis date falls close to a year boundary, the shift can move it into the adjacent year. When stratifying by diagnosis year a patient may therefore appear to sit in the wrong stratum in the table; the curves use the real year.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: ONCOcurve runs complete survival analyses entirely in your browser: Kaplan-Meier curves, the log-rank test (including weighted variants), Cox regression, and time to first treatment (TTFT). You upload oBDS XML, CSV, or Excel, filter and stratify the cohort without any coding, and export figures, tables, and a full PDF report. Every computation runs locally on your device; no patient data is transmitted. This page explains each feature step by step.

dataProcessing.title: Data processing
dataProcessing.body: Data is processed locally in your browser.

items.noTransfer: No data is transferred to a server.
items.removeData: Closing the tab clears the data.

filters.title: Filters
filters.body: Filters narrow the analysed cohort without changing the original data. All active filters are shown in the result and written into every export, so an analysis stays exactly reproducible.

items.dimensions: Filter by: sex, age group, ICD-10 code, tumour category, UICC stage, grade, primary case, year of diagnosis, and metastatic spread. Filters can be combined freely.
items.sidebar: All filters live in the left sidebar.
items.toggle: The sidebar can be collapsed and expanded via the button on the left edge.
items.responsive: On small screens (tablet, phone) the filter bar adapts.

stratification.title: Stratification (group comparison)
stratification.body: Split the cohort into groups to compare their survival curves. Pick a criterion in the sidebar; each group becomes its own coloured curve, and the log-rank test and Cox regression run automatically.

items.builtin: Built-in criteria: among others sex, age group, T, N and M category, grade, tumour entity, and entity-specific staging.
items.extra: Your own columns: any extra column from CSV or Excel (such as PAM50 or IGHV) is detected automatically as a stratification variable.
items.binning: Numeric columns (such as age or lab values) are split into groups, by quantiles (2 to 5) or manual cut-offs.
items.compare: Individual groups can be shown or hidden; the Cox reference group is freely selectable.

export.title: Export and report
export.body: Every result can be exported in full, for reports, publications, or independent re-analysis.

items.report: PDF report: via the "Download PDF report" button at the top right. Contains the analysis parameters, Kaplan-Meier curve, numbers-at-risk, landmark rates (1, 3, and 5 years), log-rank, Cox (forest plot and table), and cohort sizes. Optionally with the patient table via a checkbox. The file name includes cohort, selection, and date.
items.figures: Figures: Kaplan-Meier curve (with numbers-at-risk) and Cox forest plot as PNG and as SVG (vector graphic); the statistics card as PNG and SVG.
items.data: Data: patient table as CSV; the full analysis as an Excel workbook (curves, statistics, log-rank, Cox) for re-analysis in R or Python; Cox results additionally as separate CSV and Excel.

kaplanMeier.body: The Kaplan-Meier curve estimates survival probability over time.

items.patientsAtRisk: Patients-at-risk table is displayed below the plot.
items.plotDisplay: The „Plot display" sidebar panel allows individually toggling median lines, confidence bands, p-value, landmark table (1/3/5 years), and median follow-up display.

boxregeln.title: OncoBox calculation rules
boxregeln.body: When an OncoBox file is loaded, the curve is calculated per the specification of exactly that box. The boxes differ from one another, and those differences are not smoothed over. Curves from different boxes are therefore not directly comparable.
boxregeln.unitNote: All times from OncoBox data are days since the diagnosis date, as the specifications require. Analyses from oBDS, CSV, TXT and Excel continue to run in months.
boxregeln.estimator: The estimator is the same across all boxes: cases are sorted by time, the risk set drops by one per row, and the survival probability is the product of the factors (r minus delta) divided by r. Tied times are processed one after another, not merged. This departs from the usual convention and yields slightly different values at tied times.
boxregeln.quellenHinweis: The source line under each section names the specification and the worksheet and links to the vendor page of OnkoZert GmbH, where these files are published. The individual file has no permanent address; versions change with the audit year.
boxregeln.originBody: Every curve carries an origin note, including in the exported file. Requirement means: taken verbatim from the box's evaluation sheet. Derived means: inferred from the same box's own event definition, though that box does not prescribe a curve. Literature means: taken from the published standards for trial endpoints, not confirmed by the certifying body.

brust.title: Breast 1.0, requirement
brust.excluded: Excluded from the analysis: not tumour-free postoperatively (M1 or R1/R2), case with a relevant prior cancer, case without a dated follow-up entry. For overall survival, only the last criterion applies.
brust.event: The event is the first follow-up with local recurrence, lymph node recurrence, distant metastasis or second primary tumour. The second primary tumour is explicitly counted here, unlike in the common reading of disease-free survival.
brust.death: Anyone who dies without a recurrence enters as an event on the date of death. Without a recurrence and without a date of death, the case is censored at the last dated follow-up.

darm.title: Colorectal 1.0, requirement
darm.source: eb_darm-P1.1.1, sheets Kaplan-Meier DFS I and II and OAS I and II
darm.excluded: Excluded from the analysis: no UICC stage, UICC IV, died within 30 days of surgery, relevant prior cancer, synchronously treated further colorectal primary tumour, no complete remission (no R0 or postoperative M1a/b/c), no follow-up entry or only a life-status entry.
darm.event: The event is the first follow-up in which one of the four fields for locoregional recurrence, lymph node recurrence, distant metastasis or second primary tumour carries the value 1.
darm.death: Anyone who dies without a recurrence enters as an event, timed to the follow-up date. The box carries no date of death of its own; death is reported within the follow-up.
darm.window: The observation window ends after 5 years. Anyone without an event by then is censored at that boundary. Only the colorectal box makes this stipulation.
darm.unknown: The recurrence fields of the colorectal box know the value 2 for unknown. A case with a 2 satisfies none of the specification's three categories and is therefore excluded from the analysis. This gap is pending clarification with the certifying body.

prostata.title: Prostate 1.0, requirement
prostata.source: eb_prostata-Q1.1.1, sheets Kaplan-Meier (DFS) and (OAS) and Categories
prostata.excluded: Exclusion first branches by case type: non-interventional, interventional, or incidental finding. A non-interventional case counts outright as not tumour-free; for the others, surgery type, radiation type and margin status decide. Added to that: relevant prior cancer and a missing valid follow-up entry.
prostata.event: The event is the first follow-up with local recurrence, biochemical recurrence, metastasis or second primary tumour. No other box knows biochemical recurrence; it typically occurs well before a visible recurrence.
prostata.dates: Prostate names the event date itself, separately per event type. Time therefore runs to that date, not to the examination date. For breast and colorectal this approximation is unavoidable; here it is not.
prostata.validity: A follow-up entry only counts as valid if, for a living patient, no status field is unknown. For a deceased patient, gaps are allowed, provided a date of death is present.

familie2.title: Breast, lung and colorectal 2.0, derivation
familie2.source: Sheet EQ categories (clinical), carried over to the course of disease
familie2.note: These boxes do not prescribe a curve. Their specifications only know rates at the fixed time points of 1, 3, 5 and 10 years. The curve therefore follows from the box's own event definition, but is not itself a requirement of the certifying body.
familie2.event: Tumour-free means: residual status R0, or, in the course of disease, complete remission together with no evidence of local, lymph node or distant disease. The event is the first deviation from that, or a second primary tumour.
familie2.unknown: Entries with unknown status are skipped. They are neither a clean finding nor an event; censoring occurs at the last entry that carries a definite statement.
familie2.notTaken: Two conditions of the EQ scheme do not apply here, because they belong to the fixed-time-point logic: the tolerance window around the time point and the requirement for a current follow-up within that corridor.

weitere.title: The five endpoints without a box requirement, literature
weitere.body: Local recurrence rate, local recurrence-free survival, metastasis-free survival, progression-free survival and post-progression survival are not defined as a curve in any OncoBox specification. Their rules rest on the published standards for trial endpoints and are not confirmed by the certifying body.
weitere.rate: The local recurrence rate is calculated as cumulative incidence, not as a Kaplan-Meier curve. Anyone who dies can no longer have a local recurrence; death here is a competing event, not part of the endpoint. Kaplan-Meier treats the deceased as censored and thereby systematically overestimates the rate, for breast cancer by around 28 percent on average.
weitere.difference: This is why the rate and recurrence-free survival differ in substance too: the rate asks how many get a local recurrence, recurrence-free survival asks how long someone stays alive without one.
weitere.gap: Progression-free survival and post-progression survival are only available where the source documents a progression. Breast 1.0's overall assessment does carry the value P, but the categories of its evaluation sheet do not use it: no prescribed rule covers progression for that box. Colorectal 1.0 does not carry the field at all. That is a gap in the box, not a missing implementation.

differences.title: Where the boxes differ
differences.deathDate: Breast, prostate and the 2.0 boxes time death to the date of death; colorectal times it to the follow-up date.
differences.window: Colorectal limits the observation window to 5 years; no other box does.
differences.codes: Breast and prostate code the course-of-disease fields with letters, colorectal with digits. The same condition therefore reads differently per box.
differences.extra: Prostate additionally evaluates biochemical recurrence and names its own event dates. No other model does that.

logRank.title: Log-rank test
logRank.body: The log-rank test compares survival curves.

items.interpretation: A smaller p-value indicates stronger differences.

logRank.variantsIntro: The standard log-rank is optimal under proportional hazards. When curves cross or hazards are not proportional, weighted variants gain power by emphasising specific time regions. The variant can be selected from the Plot display sidebar.

logRank.name: Standard (Mantel-Haenszel)
logRank.when: Default; optimal under proportional hazards. Uniform weighting across all event times.

wilcoxon.name: Wilcoxon (Gehan-Breslow)
wilcoxon.when: Weights early events more heavily (n(t) declines with time). Sensitive to early differences, less so to late plateau differences.

petoPeto.name: Peto-Peto
petoPeto.when: Weights by the pooled survival function S(t) (Prentice modification). Robust variant of Wilcoxon, less sensitive to censoring patterns.

taroneWare.name: Tarone-Ware
taroneWare.when: Compromise between standard and Wilcoxon (√n(t)). All-round variant when it is unclear where differences may occur.

logRank.variantsNote: Note: choose the variant before inspecting the data, not based on which gives the smallest p-value (cherry-picking risk). When in doubt, report the standard log-rank and use weighted variants as a sensitivity analysis.

cox.title: Cox regression
cox.body: Cox regression estimates hazard ratios for stratified groups.

items.outputs: Outputs include hazard ratios and confidence intervals.
items.interpretation: Hazard ratios above 1 indicate higher risk.
items.estimation: Estimates are based on partial likelihood.
items.ties: Ties handling: Switch between Efron (default, matches R/SAS) and Breslow for simultaneous event times. Efron is more accurate when ties are common; Breslow remains available for comparison with legacy analyses.

upload.title: Upload
upload.body: Upload oBDS XML or CSV files to start analysis.

items.localSample: Use a local sample XML file.

upload.footer: Need help? Contact your data team.
upload.headerDetection: Column order is flexible. Mapping is done by column name (header). Accepted aliases per field are listed below.

optionalColumns.title: Optional columns
optionalColumns.list: gender, age, staging, grading, T/N/M, tumorCategory, primaerfall

extraColumns.title: Custom extra columns
extraColumns.intro: Any additional columns (e.g. „medication", „treatment_arm", „dose_mg") become available as stratification variables automatically.
extraColumns.numeric: Numeric columns (including with units like „mg") get a binning UI (quartile / custom cutoffs).
extraColumns.categorical: Text columns are grouped by distinct values (cap at 30 values).
extraColumns.conversion: Units are automatically converted (mass/volume/length/time) when a column contains mixed units.

ttft.title: Time to first treatment (TTFT)
ttft.intro: If your file has a firstTreatmentDate column, the tool automatically switches to the TTFT endpoint. Time then runs from first diagnosis to the first treatment (event), otherwise to the last contact (censored).
ttft.diagnosis: diagnosisDate: date of first diagnosis, used as start time t0.
ttft.treatment: firstTreatmentDate: date of the first systemic treatment, i.e. the event. Leave empty if still untreated.
ttft.lastContact: lastContactDate: last contact and censoring time. If death precedes treatment, put the date of death here.
ttft.group: IGHV or another column: any grouping to stratify, e.g. mutated and unmutated.
ttft.note: You do not need survivalTime or event, they are derived from the data. Death before treatment is censored pragmatically at death (no Fine-Gray model).

sampleFiles.intro: Every bundled sample file in one place. None of them contain real patient data, and each can be loaded straight back through the upload.

wileyStaging.body: Entity-specific staging is based on the TNM Klassifikation maligner Tumoren edited by Wittekind, 9th edition (Wiley-VCH, 2025). Not all oncological entities are included. The classification applies only to the tumour entities listed below.

anomalies.title: Anomaly warnings
anomalies.intro: Records are checked for plausibility and consistency at upload time and on the results page. Four classes are distinguished.
anomalies.uploadBehavior: Logic errors (e.g. death before diagnosis, diagnosis in the future) block the upload. A modal lists the affected records; a CSV list can be downloaded for correction in the source file. Plausibility, outliers and duplicates pass through and appear on the results page instead.
anomalies.resultsPanelTitle: What can I do on the results page?
anomalies.resultsPanel: In the anomaly panel, records are grouped by class. Each patient has a checkbox; in addition there are per-class bulk toggles and an 'Exclude all' action. Excluded patients are removed from KM, Cox, log-rank, the table and the Excel export immediately. State is persisted per dataset in sessionStorage (tab reload preserves it, a new tab does not).
anomalies.outlierNote: Outliers are computed once on the original cohort and stay static even when you exclude outliers. Otherwise the list would cascade.

upload.intro: The following records contain impossible values and must be corrected in the source file before analysis can continue.

emptyBinsWarning.title: {empty} of {total} groups are empty
emptyBinsWarning.body: Empty groups are not shown in the KM plot. Reduce the number of bins (e.g. tertile instead of quartile) or define custom cutoffs so all patients are covered.

help.quartile: Quartile (4 groups): robust, statistically established, good for exploratory analysis.
help.tertile: Tertile (3 groups): for smaller cohorts (<100) when quartile groups become too small.
help.median: Median (2 groups): simplest "low vs high" binary split.
help.manual: Custom cutoffs: when clinically established cutoffs exist.
help.rule: Rule of thumb: at least 10 patients per group for meaningful KM curves, 20+ for log-rank tests.
